summary.text: John Sununu is the Republican nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A mechanical engineer and MBA who worked in engineering, consulting and manufacturing, he served in the U.S. House from 1997 to 2003 and in the Senate from 2003 to 2009, losing his 2008 re-election bid to Jeanne Shaheen. He launched this campaign in October 2025 for the seat Shaheen is vacating.

paragraphs.text: Sununu was born in Boston, Massachusetts, in 1964. He is the son of former New Hampshire Gov. John H. Sununu (R) and the brother of former Gov. Chris Sununu (R).

He received bachelor's and master's degrees in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and an MBA from Harvard Graduate School of Business. His career before Congress included engineering, consulting and manufacturing work and running operations at an electronics company.

Sununu represented New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 1997 to 2003, serving three terms. In 2002 he defeated then-Gov. Shaheen for the U.S. Senate, and he served in the Senate from 2003 to 2009; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch.
After leaving Congress he was a faculty member at St. Anselm College and a director at Boston Scientific.
Sununu launched his 2026 campaign in October 2025, and President Trump endorsed him. He won the September 8, 2026, Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote over Scott Brown (26.4%).
His campaign website says he will oppose all middle-class tax hikes, focus on reducing inflation and the cost of housing, health care and energy, and push for term limits for Congress.
